stages.stranger: Connor Walsh, from the Aran Islands, off the west of Ireland. I fished lobster at home, and up here the storms do what I ask, mostly.
stages.acquaintance: Inis Mór, the biggest of the three islands, stone walls and wind and not a tree to be seen. I had a half-decked boat my father built and a dog called Bran who rode in the bow. My father taught me to read the sky before I could read a book.
stages.companion: My mother knitted every jumper I ever owned, and this one's the last. My father's Seán, and he still went out for the pots at seventy, God love him. Some evenings I talk to the wind in Irish and pretend it carries.
stages.friend: Weather never frightened me, and in 2017 that nearly killed a young lad on my boat. A squall came over and I laughed at it, the way I do, and he went over the side because he trusted me. I got him back, just. Now three of the Windwardens' scouts are lost in the storm over the Stormsplit, and nobody will go after them. I want to sail into it and bring them home. Will you come?
stages.sworn: We brought every one of them back, and I was frightened the whole way, properly frightened, for the first time in my life. It felt right. I wrote to that lad's mother that night, though I've no way to send it. Then I brewed the first proper pint on the tree, and it was dreadful, and the trolls loved it.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to sail into the storm with him after the lost scouts.

options.text: I'm with you, and you can be frightened with me.
options.reply: Ah, God, that's a kind thing to say. Right so, grab a rope, we're going.

options.text: It's suicide in that weather, Connor.
options.reply: It might be. That's never once stopped a fisherman going after his own.

moments.prompt: At the end of your first run he's squinting at the sky and grinning.
moments.line: Lovely weather coming tomorrow, you'll see. Rain by noon and a gale after.

options.reply: Back home that's a grand day for the pots. You'd get used to it.
Sun's grand, but it doesn't tell you anything.

lines.bored_warning: I've stood about so long I've forecast the weather three times. Let's go somewhere.
lines.leaving_good: Grand work, all of you. I'm off back to Highrest to watch the storms come in.
lines.leaving_bored: Not much doing out here, and the wind at Highrest is calling me. I'll head back.
lines.after_wipe: Up you get, slowly, and shake the water out of your ears. Then we talk it through.
lines.wipe_warning: I don't mind a storm, but this is a hurricane. We'll give it one more go and then run for harbour.
lines.wipe_leave: That's me finished for now. You'll find me out on the edge at Highrest.
lines.zone_warning: A gale's blowing and we're in a currach. Turn us round, please.
lines.zone_leave: Too rough for this crew, and I know rough. I'll be at Highrest on the Upper Boughs.
lines.gear_refuse: That one's mine, if it's all the same to you. It finally fits over the jumper.
lines.gear_taken: Go on, have it. I fished in oilskins and a wool jumper my whole life.
lines.gear_short: I wouldn't say no to something sturdier. The storms up here have teeth.
lines.gear_upgrade: Ah, that's grand, thanks a million.
lines.back: Well, look who it is! Highrest's quiet and the forecast's good. What's the plan?
lines.send_word: Connor has sent word from Highrest. The storms are quiet and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Walking off without a word isn't how I was reared. Sit down, I'll tell you straight.
lines.neglect: Ah, you're back! I'd started telling the wind to keep an eye out for you.
lines.asked_to_stay: Ah, go on so, one more. Then I'm off to watch the sky.
lines.on_break: Connor is back at Highrest on the Upper Boughs. Come back and look for them in a little while.
lines.mail_yes: Your letter blew in grand. I'll sail over to {town} and wait for you in the inn, and I'll have the first round in.
lines.mail_later: There's weather coming in at Highrest and the camp needs me. A few days and I'm yours.
lines.mail_see_me: This needs saying over a pint, not a page. Come out to Highrest and we'll talk on the edge.

town_arrive.text: Is there a pub in this town at all? I'd settle for anywhere with a fire.
Grand, a roof. I'll take it.

dungeon_clear.text: Back up into the weather, God be thanked, and none of us the worse for it.

boss_down.text: That one blew itself out. They always do, eventually.

close_call.text: Hold on to something, there's a gust coming!

zone_arrive.text: Can you smell the rain? There's a shower on the way, and a big one behind it.
